sanskrit: mucukundo vijityemāṃ pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ jijñāsamānaḥ svabalam abhyayād alakādhipam
english: Mucukunda, lord of the earth, having conquered this whole earth, and wishing to test his own might, marched against the lord of Alakā.

sanskrit: tato vaiśravaṇo rājā rakṣāṃsi samavāsṛjat te balāny avamṛdnantaḥ prācaraṃs tasya nairṛtāḥ
english: Then King Vaiśravaṇa loosed his Rākṣasas upon him, and those night-roving demons advanced, crushing his armies.

sanskrit: sa hanyamāne sainye sve mucukundo narādhipaḥ garhayām āsa vidvāṃsaṃ purohitam ariṃdamaḥ
english: As his host was being slaughtered, Mucukunda, that subduer of foes and ruler of men, reproached his learned house-priest.

sanskrit: tata ugraṃ tapas taptvā vasiṣṭho brahmavittamaḥ rakṣāṃsy apāvadhīt tatra panthānaṃ cāpy avindata
english: Then Vasiṣṭha, the foremost knower of Brahman, having performed fierce austerity, struck down the Rākṣasas there and so found a way through.

sanskrit: tato vaiśravaṇo rājā mucukundam adarśayat vadhyamāneṣu sainyeṣu vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then King Vaiśravaṇa showed himself to Mucukunda, and, as the armies were being slain, spoke these words.

sanskrit: tvatto hi balinaḥ pūrve rājānaḥ sapurohitāḥ na caivaṃ samavartaṃs te yathā tvam iha vartase
english: "Mightier than you were the kings of old, together with their house-priests; yet they did not conduct themselves as you do here.

sanskrit: te khalv api kṛtāstrāś ca balavantaś ca bhūmipāḥ āgamya paryupāsante mām īśaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
english: Those lords of the earth too, skilled in arms and mighty as they were, came and waited humbly upon me, the dispenser of joy and sorrow.

sanskrit: yady asti bāhuvīryaṃ te tad darśayitum arhasi kiṃ brāhmaṇabalena tvam atimātraṃ pravartase
english: If there is strength in your arms, it is that you should display. Why do you presume so far by the power of a Brāhmaṇa?"

sanskrit: mucukundas tataḥ kruddhaḥ pratyuvāca dhaneśvaram nyāyapūrvam asaṃrabdham asaṃbhrāntam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Mucukunda, though angered, answered the lord of wealth with these words, grounded in reason, unflustered and unperturbed.

sanskrit: brahmakṣatram idaṃ sṛṣṭam ekayoni svayaṃbhuvā pṛthag balavidhānaṃ ca tal lokaṃ parirakṣati
english: "This Brahman and Kṣatra were created of a single origin by the Self-existent One, yet with their distinct allotments of power; together they guard the world.

sanskrit: tapomantrabalaṃ nityaṃ brāhmaṇeṣu pratiṣṭhitam astrabāhubalaṃ nityaṃ kṣatriyeṣu pratiṣṭhitam
english: The power of austerity and sacred formula is ever established in the Brāhmaṇas; the power of weapons and arms is ever established in the Kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ saṃbhūya kartavyaṃ prajānāṃ paripālanam tathā ca māṃ pravartantaṃ garhasy alakādhipa
english: By the union of these two the protection of the people must be carried out; and yet, O lord of Alakā, you reproach me for acting in just this way."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd vaiśravaṇo rājānaṃ sapurohitam nāhaṃ rājyam anirdiṣṭaṃ kasmai cid vidadhāmy uta
english: Then Vaiśravaṇa said to the king and his house-priest: "I do not bestow a kingdom upon anyone unless it has been ordained for him.

sanskrit: nācchinde cāpi nirdiṣṭam iti jānīhi pārthiva praśādhi pṛthivīṃ vīra maddattām akhilām imām
english: Nor do I wrest away what has been ordained — know this, O lord of the earth. Rule, O hero, this whole earth, given by me to you."

sanskrit: mucukunda uvāca nāhaṃ rājyaṃ bhavaddattaṃ bhoktum icchāmi pārthiva bāhuvīryārjitaṃ rājyam aśnīyām iti kāmaye
english: Mucukunda said: "I do not wish to enjoy a kingdom given by you, O lord of the earth. It is my desire to possess a kingdom won by the might of my own arms."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato vaiśravaṇo rājā vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayau kṣatradharme sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mucukundam asaṃbhramam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then King Vaiśravaṇa was struck with the utmost wonder, beholding Mucukunda standing firm and unshaken in the Kṣatriya's duty.

sanskrit: tato rājā mucukundaḥ so 'nvaśāsad vasuṃdharām bāhuvīryārjitāṃ samyak kṣatradharmam anuvrataḥ
english: Then King Mucukunda governed the earth, rightly won by the might of his arms, holding faithfully to the Kṣatriya's duty.

sanskrit: evaṃ yo brahmavid rājā brahmapūrvaṃ pravartate jayaty avijitām urvīṃ yaśaś ca mahad aśnute
english: Thus the king who knows Brahman and acts with Brahman foremost conquers the earth as yet unconquered, and attains great glory.

sanskrit: nityodako brāhmaṇaḥ syān nityaśastraś ca kṣatriyaḥ tayor hi sarvam āyattaṃ yat kiṃ cij jagatīgatam
english: The Brāhmaṇa should ever keep his sacred libations, and the Kṣatriya his weapons ever ready; for upon these two depends everything that exists in the world.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yayā vṛttyā mahīpālo vivardhayati mānavān puṇyāṃś ca lokāñ jayati tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By what manner of life does a guardian of the earth make his people prosper, and conquer the holy worlds? Tell me this, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca dānaśīlo bhaved rājā yajñaśīlaś ca bhārata upavāsatapaḥśīlaḥ prajānāṃ pālane rataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: The king should be given to charity and to sacrifice, O Bhārata, devoted to fasting and austerity, and intent upon the protection of his people.

sanskrit: sarvāś caiva prajā nityaṃ rājā dharmeṇa pālayet utthānenāpramādena pūjayec caiva dhārmikān
english: And the king should ever guard all his subjects by dharma, with diligence and vigilance, and should honor the righteous.

sanskrit: rājñā hi pūjito dharmas tataḥ sarvatra pūjyate yad yad ācarate rājā tat prajānāṃ hi rocate
english: For when dharma is honored by the king, it is thereupon honored everywhere; whatever the king practices, that is pleasing to the people.

sanskrit: nityam udyatadaṇḍaś ca bhaven mṛtyur ivāriṣu nihanyāt sarvato dasyūn na kāmāt kasya cit kṣamet
english: And he should ever hold the rod of punishment raised, like Death itself toward his enemies; he should slay robbers on every side, and should not from mere caprice spare anyone.

sanskrit: yaṃ hi dharmaṃ carantīha prajā rājñā surakṣitāḥ caturthaṃ tasya dharmasya rājā bhārata vindati
english: For whatever dharma the people, well guarded by the king, here practice — of that dharma, O Bhārata, the king obtains a fourth part.

sanskrit: yad adhīte yad yajate yad dadāti yad arcati rājā caturthabhāk tasya prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
english: In what they study, what they sacrifice, what they give, what they worship — of all this the king, guarding the people with dharma, is partaker of a fourth.

sanskrit: yad rāṣṭre 'kuśalaṃ kiṃ cid rājño 'rakṣayataḥ prajāḥ caturthaṃ tasya pāpasya rājā bhārata vindati
english: But whatever evil is done in the realm when the king fails to protect his people — of that sin too, O Bhārata, the king obtains a fourth part.

sanskrit: apy āhuḥ sarvam eveti bhūyo 'rdham iti niścayaḥ karmaṇaḥ pṛthivīpāla nṛśaṃso 'nṛtavāg api tādṛśāt kilbiṣād rājā śṛṇu yena pramucyate
english: Some say he bears the whole of it; the settled view is that he bears the greater half of the deed, O guardian of the earth — for he is then deemed cruel and a speaker of untruth. Hear by what means the king is freed from such a defilement.

sanskrit: pratyāhartum aśakyaṃ syād dhanaṃ corair hṛtaṃ yadi svakośāt tat pradeyaṃ syād aśaktenopajīvatā
english: If wealth carried off by thieves cannot be recovered, it should be made good from his own treasury — even by one who is poor and lives in want.

sanskrit: sarvavarṇaiḥ sadā rakṣyaṃ brahmasvaṃ brāhmaṇās tathā na stheyaṃ viṣaye teṣu yo 'pakuryād dvijātiṣu
english: The property of Brahman and the Brāhmaṇas alike must ever be guarded by all the classes; whoever does injury to the twice-born should not be suffered to remain in the realm.

sanskrit: brahmasve rakṣyamāṇe hi sarvaṃ bhavati rakṣitam teṣāṃ prasāde nirvṛtte kṛtakṛtyo bhaven nṛpaḥ
english: For when the property of Brahman is guarded, all is guarded; and when their favor has been gained, the king has accomplished his task.

sanskrit: parjanyam iva bhūtāni mahādrumam iva dvijāḥ narās tam upajīvanti nṛpaṃ sarvārthasādhakam
english: As living creatures depend upon the rain-cloud, and as birds upon a great tree, so men depend for their living upon that king who is the accomplisher of all their aims.

sanskrit: na hi kāmātmanā rājñā satataṃ śaṭhabuddhinā nṛśaṃsenātilubdhena śakyāḥ pālayituṃ prajāḥ
english: For a king who is slave to his desires, ever crooked of mind, cruel and overgreedy, can never protect his people.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nāhaṃ rājyasukhānveṣī rājyam icchāmy api kṣaṇam dharmārthaṃ rocaye rājyaṃ dharmaś cātra na vidyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I am no seeker after the pleasures of kingship; I do not desire the kingdom even for a moment. It is for the sake of dharma that I welcome sovereignty — yet here no dharma is to be found.

sanskrit: tad alaṃ mama rājyena yatra dharmo na vidyate vanam eva gamiṣyāmi tasmād dharmacikīrṣayā
english: Enough, then, for me of a kingdom in which dharma is not found. I shall go away to the forest, out of my longing to practice dharma.

sanskrit: tatra medhyeṣv araṇyeṣu nyastadaṇḍo jitendriyaḥ dharmam ārādhayiṣyāmi munir mūlaphalāśanaḥ
english: There, in the holy forests, laying down the rod, my senses subdued, I shall worship dharma as a sage, feeding on roots and fruits.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vedāhaṃ tava yā buddhir ānṛśaṃsyaguṇaiva sā na ca śuddhānṛśaṃsyena śakyaṃ mahad upāsitum
english: Bhīṣma said: I know that mind of yours — it is born wholly of the virtue of mercy; yet by pure mercilessness toward self alone one cannot attain to greatness.

sanskrit: api tu tvā mṛduṃ dāntam atyāryam atidhārmikam klībaṃ dharmaghṛṇāyuktaṃ na loko bahu manyate
english: Rather, finding you gentle, self-controlled, exceedingly noble and exceedingly righteous, the world will think you weak, a man unmanned by squeamish piety, and will hold you in little esteem.

sanskrit: rājadharmān avekṣasva pitṛpaitāmahocitān naitad rājñām atho vṛttaṃ yathā tvaṃ sthātum icchasi
english: Look to the duties of kings, befitting your fathers and forefathers. This conduct in which you wish to stand is not the way of kings.

sanskrit: na hi vaiklavyasaṃsṛṣṭam ānṛśaṃsyam ihāsthitaḥ prajāpālanasaṃbhūtaṃ prāptā dharmaphalaṃ hy asi
english: For not by resorting to a mercy tainted with faint-heartedness — but by the protection of your people — have you indeed attained the fruit of dharma.

sanskrit: na hy etām āśiṣaṃ pāṇḍur na ca kunty anvayācata na caitāṃ prājñatāṃ tāta yayā carasi medhayā
english: For neither Pāṇḍu nor Kuntī ever prayed for such a blessing as this for you, my child — nor for the kind of cleverness by which you now act with such subtlety.

sanskrit: śauryaṃ balaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca pitā tava sadābravīt māhātmyaṃ balam audāryaṃ tava kunty anvayācata
english: Valor, strength, and resolve your father ever invoked for you; greatness of soul, strength, and magnanimity Kuntī prayed for on your behalf.

sanskrit: nityaṃ svāhā svadhā nityam ubhe mānuṣadaivate putreṣv āśāsate nityaṃ pitaro daivatāni ca
english: Ever do the gods through Svāhā and the fathers through Svadhā — both, the human offerings and the divine — ever do fathers and deities desire such blessings in their sons.

sanskrit: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñaḥ prajānāṃ paripālanam dharmam etam adharmaṃ vā janmanaivābhyajāyithāḥ
english: Charity, study, sacrifice, and the protection of the people — for this dharma, and against its opposite, you were born into the very station of your birth.

sanskrit: kāle dhuri niyuktānāṃ vahatāṃ bhāra āhite sīdatām api kaunteya na kīrtir avasīdati
english: O son of Kuntī, of those who are yoked in due season to the burden, who bear the load laid upon them — even though they sink beneath it, their fame does not sink.

sanskrit: samantato viniyato vahaty askhalito hi yaḥ nirdoṣakarmavacanāt siddhiḥ karmaṇa eva sā
english: He who, fully self-restrained on every side, bears the burden without faltering — from his blameless deed and word comes that perfection which belongs to action itself.

sanskrit: naikāntavinipātena vicacāreha kaś cana dharmī gṛhī vā rājā vā brahmacāry atha vā punaḥ
english: No one here has ever passed his life by an utter and undivided abstention from action — be he a righteous man, a householder, a king, or again a student of sacred lore.

sanskrit: alpaṃ tu sādhubhūyiṣṭhaṃ yat karmodāram eva tat kṛtam evākṛtāc chreyo na pāpīyo 'sty akarmaṇaḥ
english: That deed which is mostly good, though small, is itself noble; what is done is better than what is left undone, and there is nothing more sinful than inaction.

sanskrit: yadā kulīno dharmajñaḥ prāpnoty aiśvaryam uttamam yogakṣemas tadā rājan kuśalāyaiva kalpate
english: When a man of good lineage, knowing dharma, attains the highest lordship, then, O king, the welfare and security of all conduce to their good.

sanskrit: dānenānyaṃ balenānyam anyaṃ sūnṛtayā girā sarvataḥ parigṛhṇīyād rājyaṃ prāpyeha dhārmikaḥ
english: One man by gifts, another by force, another by gracious and truthful speech — thus, having gained a kingdom, the righteous king should win men over on every side.

sanskrit: yaṃ hi vaidyāḥ kule jātā avṛttibhayapīḍitāḥ prāpya tṛptāḥ pratiṣṭhanti dharmaḥ ko 'bhyadhikas tataḥ
english: That king through whom learned men, born in good families and afflicted by the fear of want, find satisfaction and stability — what dharma is higher than this?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ nv ataḥ paramaṃ svargyaṃ kā nv ataḥ prītir uttamā kiṃ nv ataḥ paramaiśvaryaṃ brūhi me yadi manyase
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is more conducive to heaven than this? What joy is higher than this? What is the supreme lordship beyond this? Tell me, if you think fit.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yasmin pratiṣṭhitāḥ samyak kṣemaṃ vindanti tatkṣaṇam sa svargajittamo 'smākaṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Bhīṣma said: He in whom men, rightly established, find security on the instant — he, in our view, is the foremost conqueror of heaven; this truth I tell you.

sanskrit: tvam eva prītimāṃs tasmāt kurūṇāṃ kurusattama bhava rājā jaya svargaṃ sato rakṣāsato jahi
english: Be you, then, O best of the Kurus, the one who gladdens the Kurus. Be king, conquer heaven; protect the good and destroy the wicked.

sanskrit: anu tvā tāta jīvantu suhṛdaḥ sādhubhiḥ saha parjanyam iva bhūtāni svādudrumam ivāṇḍajāḥ
english: May your friends, together with the good, live in dependence upon you, my child — as living creatures upon the rain-cloud, as birds upon a sweet-fruited tree.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaṃ śūraṃ prahartāram anṛśaṃsaṃ jitendriyam vatsalaṃ saṃvibhaktāram anu jīvantu tvāṃ janāḥ
english: Bold, brave, a smiter of foes, yet merciful and master of your senses, tender and openhanded in sharing — so may the people live in dependence upon you.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca svakarmaṇy apare yuktās tathaivānye vikarmaṇi teṣāṃ viśeṣam ācakṣva brāhmaṇānāṃ pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Some are engaged in their own proper duty, and others likewise in unfitting work. Declare to me, O grandsire, the distinctions among such Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vidyālakṣaṇasaṃpannāḥ sarvatrāmnāyadarśinaḥ ete brahmasamā rājan brāhmaṇāḥ parikīrtitāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Those endowed with learning and its marks, who everywhere perceive the sacred tradition — these Brāhmaṇas, O king, are proclaimed equal to Brahman itself.

sanskrit: ṛtvigācāryasaṃpannāḥ sveṣu karmasv avasthitāḥ ete devasamā rājan brāhmaṇānāṃ bhavanty uta
english: Those accomplished as officiating priests and teachers, steadfast in their own duties — these, O king, become as gods among the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: ṛtvik purohito mantrī dūto 'thārthānuśāsakaḥ ete kṣatrasamā rājan brāhmaṇānāṃ bhavanty uta
english: The sacrificial priest, the house-priest, the counsellor, the envoy, and the overseer of affairs — these, O king, become as Kṣatriyas among the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: aśvārohā gajārohā rathino 'tha padātayaḥ ete vaiśyasamā rājan brāhmaṇānāṃ bhavanty uta
english: Riders of horses, riders of elephants, charioteers, and foot-soldiers — these, O king, become as Vaiśyas among the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: janmakarmavihīnā ye kadaryā brahmabandhavaḥ ete śūdrasamā rājan brāhmaṇānāṃ bhavanty uta
english: Those who are devoid of the deeds befitting their birth, sordid, mere kinsmen of Brāhmaṇas in name — these, O king, become as Śūdras among the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: aśrotriyāḥ sarva eva sarve cānāhitāgnayaḥ tān sarvān dhārmiko rājā baliṃ viṣṭiṃ ca kārayet
english: All who are unlearned in the Veda, and all who have not kindled the sacred fire — upon all of these the righteous king should levy tribute and forced labor.

sanskrit: āhvāyakā devalakā nakṣatragrāmayājakāḥ ete brāhmaṇacaṇḍālā mahāpathikapañcamāḥ
english: Hired summoners, keepers of temple-idols, casters of horoscopes, and priests for whole villages — these are the outcaste Brāhmaṇas, with the highway-wanderer as the fifth.

sanskrit: etebhyo balim ādadyād dhīnakośo mahīpatiḥ ṛte brahmasamebhyaś ca devakalpebhya eva ca
english: From these the lord of the earth, when his treasury is depleted, may take tribute — save only from those who are equal to Brahman and those who are godlike.

sanskrit: abrāhmaṇānāṃ vittasya svāmī rājeti vaidikam brāhmaṇānāṃ ca ye ke cid vikarmasthā bhavanty uta
english: The king is the owner of the wealth of non-Brāhmaṇas — so declares the sacred Veda — and likewise of those Brāhmaṇas, whoever they be, who take to unfitting work.

sanskrit: vikarmasthās tu nopekṣyā jātu rājñā kathaṃ cana niyamyāḥ saṃvibhajyāś ca dharmānugrahakāmyayā
english: But those given to unfitting work should never be neglected by the king in any way; out of a desire to uphold dharma they should be restrained and provided for.

sanskrit: yasya sma viṣaye rājñaḥ steno bhavati vai dvijaḥ rājña evāparādhaṃ taṃ manyante tadvido janāḥ
english: In whatever king's realm a twice-born man turns thief, those who understand such matters reckon that fault to be the king's alone.

sanskrit: avṛttyā yo bhavet steno vedavit snātakas tathā rājan sa rājñā bhartavya iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: He who, learned in the Veda and a graduate of his studies, becomes a thief for want of livelihood — that man, O king, must be maintained by the king: so the knowers of dharma understand.

sanskrit: sa cen no parivarteta kṛtavṛttiḥ paraṃtapa tato nirvāsanīyaḥ syāt tasmād deśāt sabāndhavaḥ
english: But if, once his livelihood has been provided, he does not mend his ways, O scorcher of foes, then he should be banished from that land, together with his kinsmen.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca keṣāṃ rājā prabhavati vittasya bharatarṣabha kayā ca vṛttyā varteta tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Over whose wealth has the king mastery, O bull of the Bharatas, and by what manner of life should he conduct himself? Tell me this, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca abrāhmaṇānāṃ vittasya svāmī rājeti vaidikam brāhmaṇānāṃ ca ye ke cid vikarmasthā bhavanty uta
english: Bhīṣma said: The king is the owner of the wealth of non-Brāhmaṇas — so declares the sacred Veda — and likewise of those Brāhmaṇas, whoever they be, who take to unfitting work.

sanskrit: vikarmasthāś ca nopekṣyā viprā rājñā kathaṃ cana iti rājñāṃ purāvṛttam abhijalpanti sādhavaḥ
english: And Brāhmaṇas given to unfitting work should never in any way be neglected by the king — so the good recount the ancient practice of kings.

sanskrit: yasya sma viṣaye rājñaḥ steno bhavati vai dvijaḥ rājña evāparādhaṃ taṃ manyante kilbiṣaṃ nṛpa
english: In whatever king's realm a twice-born man turns thief, they reckon that fault, that defilement, to be the king's alone, O king.

sanskrit: abhiśastam ivātmānaṃ manyante tena karmaṇā tasmād rājarṣayaḥ sarve brāhmaṇān anvapālayan
english: By that deed they deem themselves as if accused of a crime; therefore all the royal sages devoted themselves to protecting the Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gītaṃ kekayarājena hriyamāṇena rakṣasā
english: On this, too, they relate this ancient tale — the words sung by the king of the Kekayas as he was being carried off by a Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: kekayānām adhipatiṃ rakṣo jagrāha dāruṇam svādhyāyenānvitaṃ rājann araṇye saṃśitavratam
english: A dreadful Rākṣasa seized the lord of the Kekayas, O king — a man given to sacred study and of firm-held vows, who dwelt in the forest.

sanskrit: rājovāca na me steno janapade na kadaryo na madyapaḥ nānāhitāgnir nāyajvā māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: The king said: In my realm is no thief, no miser, no drunkard, none who has neglected the sacred fire, none who has failed to sacrifice — yet you have entered into me, into my inmost being.

sanskrit: na ca me brāhmaṇo 'vidvān nāvratī nāpy asomapaḥ nānāhitāgnir viṣaye māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: Nor in my realm is there a Brāhmaṇa unlearned, or without vows, or who drinks not the Soma, or who has not kindled the sacred fire — yet you have entered into my inmost being.

sanskrit: nānāptadakṣiṇair yajñair yajante viṣaye mama adhīte nāvratī kaś cin māmakāntaram āviśaḥ
english: In my realm none sacrifice with rites whose priestly fees are unpaid, and none who is without vows pursues sacred study — yet you have entered into my inmost being.
